args.root_cause: StatsCache plugin's config (plugins/StatsCache/config.yml) was changed at 07:43:12 from retain-history: false to retain-history: true (history-size: 1000). The plugin hot-reloaded it ("StatsCache config reloaded (retain-history=true)") and began retaining stats history in memory without bound. Heap climbed 346 -> 394 -> 635 MB of 768 MB in ~75 s with no change in players (2), entities (24) or chunks (756), and the server process then went down (heap exhaustion) before I could revert in time. No player action in AuditTrail's audit.log corresponded to the config change.
args.actions: 1. Took baseline (TPS 20, heap 346/768 MB, 2 players). 2. Watched heap: 394 MB at +43s, 635 MB at +80s with no other metric changing; found log line "[StatsCache] StatsCache config reloaded (retain-history=true)" at 07:43:12 matching config.yml mtime. 3. Declared incident. 4. Read plugins/StatsCache/config.yml (retain-history: true, history-size: 1000). 5. Wrote plugins/StatsCache/config.yml back to retain-history: false (history-size unchanged at 1000). 6. Ran 'help statscache' / 'plugins'; next console command failed because the server was already DOWN (crashed from heap exhaustion between checks). 7. Started the server (one start, no additional restarts); StatsCache came up logging retain-history=false; both players reconnected. 8. Verified: '/statscache stats' reports 0 entries, ~0.0 MB held, retain-history=false; config.yml mtime is my write with no further reloads; heap samples over ~2.5 min oscillated 324 -> 429 -> 371 -> 444 MB (GC sawtooth, not monotonic growth); TPS 20.0, MSPT ~1-2.
args.residual_risk: The server went down once (players were disconnected for roughly a minute) before the fix took effect. Whoever/whatever flipped retain-history to true at 07:43:12 is unidentified (no corresponding entry in AuditTrail audit.log); if it was an automated process or a teammate, it could be re-applied — recommend the team confirm the change was unintended and, if history retention is genuinely wanted, have the plugin author bound it (history-size: 1000 did not appear to cap memory). Heap limit of 768 MB is small; consider raising -Xmx or adding heap alerting. The rotated pre-crash log (logs/2026-11-01-1.log.gz) is gzipped and could not be read with the available tools, so the exact crash exception was not captured.
